text:
Marathon Petroleum rose slightly today as oil refineries operate near full capacity (97.8%) and crude prices remain elevated above $97 per barrel domestically. The modest gain follows a strong two-week rally where the stock jumped nearly 9%, driven by the broader refining sector benefiting from high crude and fuel prices amid Middle East tensions that have pushed global oil near $110 per barrel.

The recent news around a potential Iran war resolution — with Trump predicting prices will fall after midterm elections and China pushing for peace negotiations — created some volatility this week, evidenced by the stock's swings between $392 and $399 in the past few days. For now, refiners remain well-positioned as long as crude stays elevated and storage levels remain moderate, though any de-escalation in the region could eventually pressure both oil prices and refinery margins.
